title: Relative pseudo-coherence is local on the source
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes which is locally of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions], let $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category], let $m\in\mathbf Z$, and let $X=\bigcup_{k\in I}X_k$ be a covering by open subschemes, with an arbitrary index set $I$. For each $k$ let $f_k=f|_{X_k}:X_k\to S$ and let $E|_{X_k}=L\iota_k^*E$ be the derived pullback [def-pc-derived-pullback] along the inclusion $\iota_k:X_k\to X$. If, for every $k$, $E|_{X_k}$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $S$ with respect to $f_k$ [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex], then $E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $S$ with respect to $f$. Consequently, if every $E|_{X_k}$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $S$, then so is $E$. No quasi-compactness of $X$, $S$ or $f$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09UJ, lemma-relative-pseudo-coherence-characterize: (1) => (2) for each E|_{X_k}, then (2) => (1) for E using an affine open covering of each f^{-1}(V_i) by affines contained in some X_k; this is the locality used in the first paragraph of the proof of Tag 0CSL ('show that K is pseudo-coherent relative to A in a neighbourhood of x and this will prove the lemma').

proof.text: Fix $m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], choose an affine open cover $S=\bigcup_{a\in A}V_a$. For each $a,k$, let $\mathcal U_{ak}$ be the set of all affine opens of $X$ contained in $X_k\cap f^{-1}(V_a)$. These form a set, since opens are subsets of the underlying set of $X$. They cover that intersection: for any point in it, the affine-basis statement supplies such a neighbourhood. Since the $X_k$ cover $X$, the family indexed by all pairs $(k,U)$ with $U\in\mathcal U_{ak}$ covers $f^{-1}(V_a)$. No intersection of affine opens is asserted to be affine.

source.place: Tag 09UJ, lemma-relative-pseudo-coherence-characterize, affine-cover characterization; schemes.tex Tag 01IT, lemma-basis-affine-opens

proof.text: The restriction $f_k=f\circ\iota_k$ is locally of finite type [def-pc-morphism-conventions, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], as the hypothesis on $f_k$ presupposes: for an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $S$, cover $f^{-1}(V)$ by affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ a finitely generated $A$-algebra; the principal opens $D(g)\subset\operatorname{Spec}B\cap X_k$ cover $f_k^{-1}(V)$, and $B_g=B[1/g]$ is generated over $A$ by the generators of $B$ and $1/g$. For every $a,k$ and $U\in\mathcal U_{ak}$, apply [lem-sfb-relative-pseudocoherence-all-affine-charts] to the assumed relative $m$-pseudo-coherence of $E|_{X_k}$ for $f_k:X_k\to S$, with affine opens $U\subset X_k$ and $V_a\subset S$. It supplies a closed immersion $j_{akU}:U\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{n_{akU}}_{V_a}$ and says that $R(j_{akU})_*((E|_{X_k})|_U)$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent. Here $(E|_{X_k})|_U=E|_U$: for an open inclusion $h$, $\mathcal O_U=h^{-1}\mathcal O_X$, so the formula in [def-pc-derived-pullback] reduces to ordinary termwise restriction (derived tensor with the unit ring sheaf is the identity); restriction through two nested opens is the direct restriction. Thus the displayed pushforward is $R(j_{akU})_*(E|_U)$.

source.place: Tag 09UJ, implication (1) to (2); Tag 09VC, lemma-relatively-pseudo-coherent, existence of an affine-space embedding

proof.text: The affine base cover $\{V_a\}$, the source covers $\{U\}_{(k,U)}$ of step 1, and the embeddings with the pushforward property of step 2 are exactly the witnesses in [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex]. They therefore prove that $E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $S$. The witnesses on different opens need no transition maps: the definition asks only for their existence.

If every $E|_{X_k}$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $S$, then for each integer $m$ every restriction is relatively $m$-pseudo-coherent, by [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Applying steps 1--3 separately for this $m$ proves the relative $m$-condition for $E$. Quantifying over $m$ gives relative pseudo-coherence of $E$. Covers and embeddings may vary with $m$, as the definition permits; neither a finite subcover nor a common cohomological bound is required.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09UJ, lemma-relative-pseudo-coherence-characterize, implication (1) to (2), followed by the covering definition in Tag 09UI; this justifies the neighbourhood reduction at the start of Tag 0CSL, lemma-characterize-pseudo-coherent.
